title: quick accent inserts `」` as `「` in the wechat desktop app
author: brauljo
summary: Quick Accent is reported to select the closing corner bracket `」`, while WeChat Desktop receives the opening bracket `「`; the attached diagnostics confirm Quick Accent is enabled but do not prove whether PowerToys emits the wrong code point or WeChat transforms keyboard-style Unicode input.

status.label: Reproduction before design
status.detail: The investigator/adversary pass found the report testable but not yet implementation-designable because the root cause depends on a WeChat-versus-neutral-target comparison.

next_action.label: Reproduce Quick Accent in WeChat
next_action.reason: Capture the selected character, emitted code point, receiving-app result, and whether clipboard paste of U+300D behaves differently.

judgment.rationale: The issue provides a specific expected/actual character pair, target application, and diagnostic archive, so it is ready for maintainer reproduction. A fix design should not be approved yet because the current evidence does not distinguish a Quick Accent mapping/injection defect from WeChat or IME smart-punctuation handling of KEYEVENTF_UNICODE input.
evidence: The report says selecting/typing `」` through Quick Accent in WeChat Desktop produces `「` instead.
The attached PowerToysReport_2026-09-02-10-15-48.zip shows PowerToys v0.100.2 and QuickAccent enabled.
CharacterMappings.cs maps Pinyin VK_COMMA to `“`, `”`, `‘`, `’`, `「`, `」`, `『`, `』`, so both bracket code points are present and adjacent in the data.
PowerAccent.cs passes the selected string to WindowsFunctions.Insert, and WindowsFunctions.cs sends each UTF-16 code unit via SendInput with KEYEVENTF_UNICODE after optional backspace.
No duplicate issue or linked fix was found for the WeChat bracket substitution, and the timeline has no assignee or maintainer direction.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a controlled reproduction in WeChat and a neutral text control, and compare SendInput Unicode insertion with clipboard paste before designing a compatibility change.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent insertion of U+300D is reported as U+300C specifically in WeChat Desktop.
known_information: The desired character is `」` (U+300D) and the received character is `「` (U+300C).
The affected application is WeChat Desktop.
The reporter supplied a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP; it confirms QuickAccent is enabled on PowerToys v0.100.2.
The Pinyin comma mapping contains both `「` and `」`, and the insertion helper sends the selected string through KEYEVENTF_UNICODE SendInput.
inferences: If a neutral text control receives U+300D correctly, the most likely failure is WeChat or an active IME transforming keyboard-style Unicode input.
If multiple applications receive U+300C when U+300D is selected, the selected index, mapping order, or Quick Accent handoff is more likely involved.
Clipboard paste may bypass application keyboard smart-punctuation logic, but using it as a default fallback would have clipboard-state and security/UX tradeoffs.
issue_context.analysis: Investigation found a plausible PowerToys insertion path but not a proven root cause. The adversary pass blocks an implementation-grade design because the same symptom could persist or disappear depending on WeChat’s handling of Unicode key events versus pasted text.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the live issue body, attachment, comments, labels, assignees, timeline, and closed-by-PR references.
Downloaded and inspected the diagnostic ZIP; QuickAccent is enabled and no Quick Accent SendInput error was found in the relevant logs.
Searched current issues for Quick Accent, WeChat, and bracket substitutions; only this issue matched directly.
Inspected CharacterMappings.cs, PowerAccent.cs, WindowsFunctions.cs, KeyboardListener.cpp, and CharacterMappingsTests.cs in the local PowerToys clone.
Investigator conclusion: likely failure is in target-app handling of KEYEVENTF_UNICODE or in selection/handoff, but evidence does not distinguish them.
Adversary conclusion: no approval-gate design should be written until a neutral-target comparison proves which side changes the code point.

design_review.investigator: The code can emit the selected Pinyin bracket through WindowsFunctions.Insert using KEYEVENTF_UNICODE, and WeChat-specific transformation is plausible.
design_review.adversary: Blocking objection: the issue lacks a neutral target or instrumentation proving whether PowerToys emits U+300D and WeChat changes it, or PowerToys selects/emits U+300C.

reproduce.version_requirements: Use PowerToys 0.100.2 if available, then retest on the current build.
prerequisites: Notepad or another plain Win32 text control
Quick Accent configured with the Pinyin character set containing `」`
steps: Open Notepad and use the same Quick Accent gesture to select `」`; record the glyph and Unicode code point inserted.
Repeat the identical selection in WeChat Desktop; record whether WeChat inserts `」` or `「`.
If Notepad receives `」` but WeChat receives `「`, paste `」` into WeChat from the clipboard and record whether paste preserves U+300D.
If both apps receive `「`, enable Quick Accent Unicode descriptions and record which item/index is highlighted before release.
Collect a fresh `/bugreport` immediately after the reproduction if the current build still differs between targets.
reproduce.expected_result: Selecting `」` should insert U+300D consistently in both applications.
setup_requirements: Use the same keyboard layout, IME mode, Quick Accent language set, and trigger gesture for both targets.
